title: The $\ell$-adic diagonal class over the completed coefficient sheaf
statement:
With the notation of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]:

1. $R\varprojlim_n\Delta_*\mathbf Z/\ell^n=\Delta_*\Zl$ and
   $R\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/\ell^n(1)=\Zl(1)$, and more generally derived
   direct image along any morphism of the pro-étale sites considered commutes
   with $R\varprojlim$ and is computed levelwise on inverse systems.
2. The Tate twist $(1)$, defined as tensor product over the completed
   coefficient sheaf with the invertible sheaf $\Zl(1)$ (and $(-1)$ with its
   dual), is exact, preserves products and commutes with $R\varprojlim$.
3. $R\varprojlim c_\bullet$ is a morphism
   $\delta_{\Zl}:\Delta_*\Zl\to\Zl(1)[2]$ of derived $\ell$-complete objects; it
   is the derived $\ell$-completion of $\partial$, and it is in a unique way a
   morphism in $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\Zl)$ over the completed coefficient sheaf
   $\Zl$ of $W$. Its reductions modulo $\ell^n$ are the torsion cycle classes.

proof.text: The finite completed-coefficient components form a cone: the constant inverse-image comparison is natural in each quotient ring homomorphism. Compose this natural transformation with the inverse-image of the canonical limit cone and use the limit projection equation. This proves diagonalCompletedCoefficient_naturality.

On the diagonal site the integer-to-unit section map is a presheaf natural transformation, since ring restrictions preserve integer casts. Extend it by sheafification and push it forward along the closed diagonal. The closed adjunction counit is invertible, so every candidate has a unique preimage; the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction at the terminal object shows that the prescribed integer values determine that preimage. This proves diagonalCompletedGenerator_existsUnique.

Restriction of scalars preserves finite limits and colimits because its composite with the faithful exact underlying additive-sheaf functor is the source underlying functor. Compose the two restrictions with the constant-ring module-sheaf equivalence to obtain exactness and additivity of diagonalCompletedRestriction. The direct-image and completed-limit theorem proofs retain the plan below.

For diagonalTower_directImage, work directly with the fixed-scalar module-sheaf categories. Their Grothendieck property and the strict-tower Grothendieck argument supply K-injective resolutions. Use the total derived data construction underlying lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit to package the four triangulated right derived functors. Define each derived-limit projection by rightDerivedDesc; its universal equation gives normalization on complexes. The two evaluation composites have units with the same source and are invertible on K-injective towers, since exact evaluation preserves K-injectives. Uniqueness of right derived functors gives the normalized evaluation isomorphisms. The exact inverse-image/direct-image adjunction, whiskered to towers, makes the levelwise direct image preserve K-injectives. It preserves ordinary limits as a right adjoint. Apply the generic composite comparison underlying lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison to obtain the limit isomorphism normalized by limit.post. Finally use rightDerived_ext on the common composite: after precomposing with its unit, the desired projection equation follows from the comparison unit equation, naturality of the target projection, the evaluation unit equation, limit.post composed with a projection, and the source projection normalization. This proves compatibility with every canonical derived projection, not merely existence of some isomorphism.

The published locally free cover of the completed Tate line gives the covering sieves of its local unit trivializations. The line-evaluation inverse pair gives tensor by this line and by its dual as equivalences, hence additive and exact. Flat-single derived normalization identifies the fixed derived tensor with the derived exact tensor equivalence, compatibly with its shift. An equivalence preserves products, and the normalized homotopy-limit comparison is invertible by the equivalence limit API in FormalClosedSupportIILimits. Apply this to d = 1 and d = -1. This proves diagonalCompletedTwist_limits.

Use the proved diagonal_limit_typed_data to assemble the strict and completed data in the definitionally identical named specification. Apply diagonalLimitSpec_of_typed to obtain the original DiagonalCompletedLimitSpec. All original theorem signatures are unchanged. The typed assembly contains the actual combining argument and introduces no additional proof obligation.

split_report.summary: Continued the inherited sandbox against the current shared DAG; retained its statement, proof route, citations and recorded searches. Divided the three long proof paragraphs into seven explicit steps without adding nodes. Checked every cited statement, constant versus completed coefficient rings, finite-ring exactness for each transition, the identity-immersion specialization of the tensor-limit tool, and naturality of finite reductions. No exact project Lean attachment or Mathlib theorem states the item. No new nodes or leaves.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-3 realize main-20261015 limit proof paragraph (1); step 4 realizes paragraph (2); steps 5-7 realize paragraph (3), with explicit finite-reduction naturality and the constant/completed coefficient comparison. The item is not the key statement of its unit, so no unit realized field is changed.

tool_uses.why: The item needs the generic fact that epimorphic coefficient towers have no R^1 inverse-limit term; the diagonal-tower unit does not provide this categorical limit theorem.

The item needs levelwise derived direct image and its Rlim comparison for towers of constant Z_l-modules along arbitrary morphisms; this generic ringed-topos statement covers that coefficient category, which the completed-coefficient tower node of the proper base change unit does not.
Fixes the total derived inverse limit of strict towers (with its Roos triangle) used by the ringed-topos tower comparison; generic, no diagonal-unit node gives it.
The item uses the general definition and local rank-one property of Tate twists to identify the tensor functor.
The item needs the generic finite-locally-free tensor preservation of products, fibers and derived inverse limits.
The item needs the constant/completed coefficient equivalence on derived complete objects to obtain unique completed-coefficient linearity.
The item needs finite reduction of a derived inverse-limit tower to its level term in order to identify reductions of the completed class.
Generic exactness of closed pro-etale direct image over a finite ring preserves each coefficient transition epimorphism; the diagonal unit does not supply this sheaf-theoretic fact.

Generic roots-of-unity transition surjectivity and local rank-one freeness over the completed coefficient sheaf, specialized to E=Q_l; this verifies the hypotheses of the Milnor and finite-locally-free tensor tools.

Its explicit finite-reduction and completion-unit comparisons identify reductions and completeness over constant and completed coefficients; the diagonal unit does not supply those generic scalar-restriction identities.
The generic integral coefficient identification, specialized to E=Q_l, identifies the inverse limit of finite constant quotients with the pulled-back completed coefficient sheaf on W.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q138-0ed46a688 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all seven steps, every cited statement (13 proof deps plus det-pe-milnor-sequence, lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit, def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum, sk-def-sfb-dc-setting and sk-lem-formal-closed-support), the unit record and the main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof (1)-(3). In Stacks I checked tags 099L/099M/099I/0A07/093M against tags/tags, and read 0A07 (sites-cohomology l.5150) and 099I (algebraization l.1427). The statement is the verbatim blueprint text and was not changed. There are no new nodes and no SGA sources. Step 1: the towers are epimorphic (lem-pur (1), l invertible on W). det-pe-milnor-epimorphic with the constant Z_l ring gives lim = Rlim, and its cone convention agrees with the total derived Rlim because pro-étale products are derived products. The limits are the completed sheaf (integral-limit (3), E=Q_l) and Zl(1). Step 2: the complement of the diagonal is locally D(t), so it is quasi-compact. lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact over Z/l^(n+1) keeps the transitions epimorphic, and Delta_* commutes with lim. Step 3: the ringed-topos tower comparison (any morphism of ringed topoi, no ring identification needed) gives the levelwise and Rlim statements for constant Z_l towers. Step 4: Zl(1) and its dual are locally free of rank one, and the tensor clause of det-formal-closed-support-ii-limits with X=Z=S=W, identity immersions and empty complement gives products, fibers and Rlim. Steps 5-6: system (2)-(4) together with lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction (Lambda=Z_l, I=(l), F_l torsion, Z/l^n perfect, K = Delta_*Z ⊗ Z_l and G_m[1] ⊗ Z_l) identify the reductions of the morphism itself with c_n, by naturality. Step 7: lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence compares the reductions and the completion units, and the equivalence on complete objects gives a unique Zl-linear lift. Repair (one E1-type unchecked hypothesis): steps 4 and 7 applied det-formal-closed-support-ii-limits and sk-lem-integral-models, which are stated only in the standing setting, without saying that W is in it. Steps 4 and 7 now state that W lies in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] (already an item stmt_dep): Y is in that setting and P^1_Y and W are projective over Y. sk-def-sfb-dc-setting is added to their uses and proof_deps is recomputed. There is no cycle: a DFS over all dependencies does not reach the item. theorem diagonalTower_limit (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (hpℓ : p ≠ ℓ)
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hY : IsUnit (ℓ : Γ(Y, ⊤)))
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalAb (diagonalSurface Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalMod ℓ (diagonalSurface Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalSystems ℓ (diagonalSurface Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb (diagonalSurface Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalCompleted ℓ (diagonalSurface Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalCompleted ℓ (diagonalSurface Y))]
    [HasExt.{u + 1} (DiagonalSystems ℓ (diagonalSurface Y))]
    (D : DiagonalDerivedReduction ℓ (diagonalScalarExtension ℓ (diagonalSurface Y)))
    (hcompletion : DiagonalCompletionSpec ℓ (diagonalSurface Y) D)
    (hsystem : DiagonalCycleSystemSpec ℓ Y hY D) :
  DiagonalCompletedLimitSpec ℓ Y hY D
lean.note: The three clauses are stated as diagonalTower_limit, diagonalTower_directImage and diagonalCompletedTwist_limits. Actual coefficient restriction, ordinary-to-derived limit maps, normalized quotient units, and the positive Cartier boundary fix the full completed-coefficient arrow; no uniqueness from separate reductions is asserted.
